previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Thompson was admitted for a right ureteral stone requiring surgical intervention. Given his mechanical aortic valve and chronic anticoagulation with Coumadin, he was admitted early for a heparin bridge. He underwent right ureteroscopy with laser lithotripsy and stent placement on January 19 without complications. Postoperatively, he was transitioned back to Coumadin with overlapping heparin until his INR reached the therapeutic range of 2.5–3.5. His hospital course was uncomplicated, with stable management of comorbidities including diastolic heart failure, COPD, diabetes, and coronary artery disease. He was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to follow up with his PCP for INR monitoring and urology for stent removal.

nonadherence. He was started on a heparin drip and given

Discharge Instructions:
You were admitted to the hospital because you missed several 
coumadin dosages.  Your INR was not therapeutic.  You were 
administered an intravenous anticoagulant until your INR became 
therapeutic.  Please resume you home coumadin regimen.
.
Please keep all followup appointments. 
 
. 
 
Please call your doctor or return to the emergency room if you 
have any of the following: 
 
* You experience new chest pain, pressure, squeezing or 
 
tightness. 
 
* New or worsening cough or wheezing. 
 
* If you are vomiting and cannot keep in fluids or your 
 
medications. 
 
* You are getting dehydrated due to continued vomiting, 
 
diarrhea or other reasons. Signs of dehydration include dry 
 
mouth, rapid heartbeat or feeling dizzy or faint when standing. 
 
* You see blood or dark/black material when you vomit or have a 
 
bowel movement. 
 
* Your pain is not improving within ___ hours or not gone 
 
within 24 hours. Call or return immediately if your pain is 
 
getting worse or is changing location or moving to your chest or 

 
back. 
 
* You have shaking chills, or a fever greater than 101.5 (F) 
 
degrees or 38(C) degrees. 
 
* Any serious change in your symptoms, or any new symptoms that 
 
concern you. 
 
* Please resume all regular home medications and take any new 
meds 
 
as ordered.
